title: Slider Shot
description: A slider shot is a short, precise linear move on a compact rail, often 60 to 120 centimeters. It adds parallax to an interview, product, or lock-off without a full dolly track.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: A full dolly is too much. A few centimeters of travel can prove the room has depth: a microphone in the foreground slides against a face, a bottle turns against a window.
The move is small on purpose. It is the wrong tool for a city block, and the wrong tool if you needed a curve around a product.
If the rail is meters long, you are dollying. If the path is a circle, you are orbiting.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Clamp a short rail, level it, choose a constant speed. Keep the move lateral or a tiny push; do not hide a zoom inside it.
Prompt a short slider move, 60 to 120 centimeters of lateral travel, product or interview parallax, precise and small.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when a full dolly is too much and a lock-off needs a little parallax. Concrete beat: an interview single with a lamp sliding in the foreground over 6 seconds.
Do not slider a chase.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: A Dolly Left is the same linear idea at room or street scale. An 360-Degree Orbit is curved and long.
A Push In may use a slider as the rail, but push in is the Z-axis thought; slider names the short linear tool. Slider is compact travel, not a path through architecture.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The grammar is commercial and interview more than a single famous scene: tabletop product films, documentary talking heads, small table moves inside features. Use the 60-to-120-centimeter parallax, not a particular ad to clone.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a full Dolly Left or a tiny 360-Degree Orbit. The tell is meters of travel, or a curve.
The fix: name the short rail, linear path, subtle parallax, end still in the same room.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Slider Shot in film?
It is a short linear camera move on a compact rail, typically under about 120 centimeters, used to add small parallax to a still setup.
Slider Shot vs Dolly Left
Dolly left can travel a room or a street. A slider is the compact rail version: interview, product, a lamp sliding against a face.
When should I use Slider Shot?
When a lock-off feels dead and a full track would be too much. Do not use it as a substitute for covering a walk.
How do I prompt Slider Shot for AI image or video?
Write short slider, 60 to 120 centimeters, lateral, subtle parallax, 6 seconds. Ban a long dolly and ban a circular orbit.
